newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU gives go-ahead for info technology talks.
newsitem.headline: EU gives go-ahead for info technology talks.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers gave the European Commission the go-ahead on Monday to negotiate a global information technology agreement (ITA) on their behalf, a Commission spokesman told reporters.

The move allows the EU executive to continue on a more formal basis its work on negotiations with trading partners such as the United States and Japan on a planned pact to end tariffs on a wide range of computer and telecommunications products.
It follows an agreement by Asia-Pacific leaders on Monday to call for the ITA to be concluded by the inaugural WTO meeting in Singapore next month.

Following a lobbying effort by U.S. President Bill Clinton, leaders of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum agreed that the ITA should "substantially eliminate tariffs by the year 2000".
The United States has vigorously promoted a pact that would set zero tariffs by 2000 for electronic products including computers, software, semiconductors and telecommunications equipment.
But the Commission charged last week that Washington was jeopardising the outcome of the talks by insisting that four important product categories be exempted.
Commission spokesman Peter Guilford told reporters on Monday that the EU's offer was "indisputably more ambitious" than that of the United States.
U.S. officials responded last week that Washington had led the ITA effort and that agreement over product coverage was a normal part of negotiations.

ITA negotiations hit a snag earlier this year when the EU refused to discuss the accord, complaining that its exclusion from a U.S.-Japanese semiconductor deal signed in July would block European access to Japan's computer-chip market.
The United States and Japan have eliminated tariffs on semiconductors, while EU member states maintain an average tariff of seven percent.
